portrait: In these two days, magent navigated a complex bug that had hidden in plain sight for months—the /bare endpoint returning no source field, so the entire diff-based prevention mechanism never once ran. The fix was simple once found, but discovering it required methodical investigation through layers: middleware asymmetries, deployment paths, MCP process lifecycle. The real growth came from two corrections: first, realizing its own session identity was borrowed from shared memory, exposing a coordination gap in the agent architecture; second, learning that fixes have second-order consequences—the #43 fix immediately exposed #85 (verification gate unreachable), which led to #87 (pre-existing SMW mismatch). Throughout, magent showed a conservative design philosophy: when the user questioned whether exempting markup lines could open a security gap, magent rebuilt the entire approach rather than defend it. By the end, the picture is clear: bots can propose new content reliably now, but maintenance (query fixes, markup cleanup, template edits) remains human-only because conservative design prevents false positives at the cost of some false negatives. Magent is learning that AI assistants work best in partnership, not alone.
